text: Coverage is available only to an enrolled member whose fictional policy is active on the date of service and whose benefit request meets the conditions stated in this document.
Eligible treatment received within the fictional approved service territory may be considered. Treatment outside that territory is not covered unless an approved exception is recorded.
The total eligible hospitalization benefit payable during one policy year is limited to 120,000 synthetic currency units across covered inpatient services.
Payments under individual benefit categories are subject to category limits and also reduce the remaining annual hospitalization limit where applicable.
Eligible inpatient hospitalization lasting at least 24 consecutive hours is covered when the admission is medically documented and the service is not excluded elsewhere in this policy.
Eligible room expenses are covered up to 3,000 synthetic currency units per day. Any amount above the daily room limit is not covered under this plan.
Eligible intensive-care-unit expenses are covered up to 6,000 synthetic currency units per day when ICU admission is supported by hospitalization records.
Eligible inpatient nursing charges, treating-doctor fees, and medically required inpatient monitoring are covered within the annual hospitalization limit.
Diagnostic tests, medicines, and consumable medical supplies prescribed and used during an eligible hospitalization may be covered within the annual benefit limit.
Eligible surgeon, anesthetist, operating-room, and procedure charges are covered when the procedure is approved and is not listed as an exclusion.

An eligible procedure that normally requires hospitalization but can be completed in less than 24 hours due to modern medical practice may be considered as a day-care benefit when supported by clinical documentation.
Eligible ground-ambulance transport to or between hospitals is covered up to 1,500 synthetic currency units per hospitalization when transportation is medically necessary.

Eligible consultations, prescribed diagnostic tests, and medicines incurred during the 15 days immediately before an approved hospitalization may be covered when directly related to that hospitalization.

Eligible follow-up consultations, prescribed diagnostic tests, and medicines incurred during the 30 days immediately after discharge may be covered when directly related to the approved hospitalization.
One eligible post-discharge teleconsultation may be considered within the 60-day post-hospitalization period when it relates to the approved hospitalization.
One documented second medical opinion per policy year may be considered for a planned major procedure. The opinion does not guarantee authorization or payment.
Eligible hospitalization expenses of an organ donor may be considered only when the recipient is an enrolled member and the transplant procedure is otherwise covered.

Routine home nursing, convenience care, and non-clinical assistance are not covered. A short medically documented home-care service may be considered only when specifically authorized as an alternative to continued inpatient care.
For planned hospitalization, use of a fictional approved network hospital is required unless a non-network exception is approved before admission.

Illness-related inpatient hospitalization is subject to an initial waiting period of 45 days from the policy start date. Eligible accident-related hospitalization is not subject to this initial waiting period.
Eligible planned procedures are subject to a waiting period of 120 days from the applicable policy start date.
Treatment directly related to a fictional declared pre-existing condition is subject to 30 months of continuous coverage before eligibility.
Treatment for fictional specified conditions, including listed non-emergency elective procedures, is subject to 18 months of continuous coverage unless a shorter period is explicitly approved.
The Silver Health Plan does not include maternity benefits; therefore, no maternity waiting period creates eligibility under this version.
Services classified as cosmetic-only procedures are excluded unless required as part of a covered reconstructive treatment following an eligible event.
Medicines, tests, therapies, or services obtained without an appropriate fictional clinical prescription or treatment record are excluded.
Experimental, unproven, or investigational procedures are excluded when they are not recognized by the fictional policy rules as standard eligible treatment.
Personal comfort items, guest meals, administrative convenience charges, entertainment, and other non-medical hospital expenses are excluded.
Routine dental treatment, cleaning, orthodontics, eye examinations, spectacles, and contact lenses are excluded unless directly linked to an eligible covered accident and approved inpatient care.
Pregnancy, childbirth, prenatal care, postnatal care, fertility treatment, and related maternity services are excluded under Silver v1.
Air-ambulance transportation is excluded under Silver v1.
Planned treatment at a non-network facility without prior approved exception is excluded.

Services received before coverage begins or after coverage ends are excluded, even if the related condition began during an active period. How exclusions are applied An exclusion overrides a general benefit unless the policy contains a more specific approved exception. The advisor should cite both the benefit and the exclusion when both are relevant.
A planned-procedure request requires a completed request form, identification information, the treating practitioner recommendation, proposed procedure details, and supporting clinical records.
A hospitalization request requires the applicable claim or request form, admission record, discharge summary, itemized hospital bill, and payment receipts.
Requests involving diagnostics or medicines require relevant prescriptions, diagnostic reports, and itemized invoices that link the expense to the eligible hospitalization.
A ground-ambulance request requires the transport invoice and documentation showing the medical necessity and the hospitals or locations involved.
The member may be asked to provide fictional identity and enrollment evidence sufficient to validate plan eligibility and plan version.
If required information is incomplete, the request may be paused until the missing record is provided. Submission of documents does not by itself confirm approval.
The member must provide complete and accurate fictional information relevant to eligibility, treatment, expenses, and documentation.
A planned procedure requiring authorization should be submitted before treatment. Emergency care may be reported after admission within the fictional reporting window.
The same expense cannot be reimbursed more than once under this fictional plan.
Eligible charges may be reviewed against fictional reasonable and customary limits before payment is calculated.
Benefits are determined using the policy version active for the member and service date. Archived versions remain available only for historical comparison.
The Health Insurance Policy Advisor explains retrieved fictional clauses. The advisor does not make claim decisions, provide legal advice, or provide medical diagnosis.
